specs.source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/README.md §0.4 'Chips' and 'Workspace tags'; 'Caros Ledge UI System.dc.html' #sys 'Chips — three kinds, three shapes' block; operator ruling 2.5
notes: Chips.tsx is pure inline style (media queries only affect <768px, not this 1440 mount); every property here is a real product value.

Ruling 2.5 restates the family rules (band = tinted pill + round dot; workspace tag = square dot, removable; kind/mode/topic = neutral, no dot, no border; tier = the only bordered chip) without new numbers for band/tier/tag beyond what the artboard states, so the artboard markup is the numeric source for those three.

TagChip has no `border` set at all (correct per ruling 2.5's 'no dot, NO border'); the artboard's neutral tag also has no border rule. Both sides agree, not asserted as a property since 'unset' has no single canonical getComputedStyle form worth comparing.

CONFIRMED, verified not a harness artefact: `--radius-pill` computes to nothing (CSSOM initial value, 0) in the real product, not just this harness. src/app/theme.css declares it TWICE inside the SAME plain `:root{}` rule (no `@theme` involved, no Tailwind step in play): line 55 `--radius-pill: 999px;`, then line 201 `--radius-pill: var(--radius-pill);` — a property declared in terms of itself, which CSS defines as invalid, and the invalid LATER declaration wins over the valid earlier one within one rule (there is no 'fall back to the earlier declaration' in CSS custom properties). Every chip that reads `var(--radius-pill)` — BandChip, WorkspaceTagPill, and TagChip (see next note) — renders SQUARE corners everywhere in the shipped product, not just in this measurement. Confirmed by probing `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--radius-pill')` directly against theme.css alone (empty string) before writing this spec.

TagChip's radius is a second, separate issue on top of the broken token: even if `--radius-pill` were fixed to 999px, the artboard's neutral tag uses `border-radius:4px` (a squared tag, matching the tier chip's own 4px-square convention), not a pill — TagChip.tsx reaches for the pill token where the design wants the square one.

FIXED by fix58-tokens (2026-09-07): removed theme.css's self-referential `--radius-pill: var(--radius-pill);` redeclaration (it carried no independent value and only broke the earlier valid one); `--radius-pill` now resolves to 999px sitewide. TagChip.tsx also switched to `border-radius:4px` (the design's square-tag value, not the pill token).

SITEWIDE FINDING, confirmed live (not a harness artefact): both filter-chip border-radius checks below measure 0px against theme.css's own --radius-pill:999px token. Root cause, confirmed by reading src/app/theme.css line 213: `--radius-pill: var(--radius-pill);` — a CUSTOM PROPERTY THAT REFERENCES ITSELF inside the same :root block that first declares `--radius-pill: 999px` at line 55. Per the CSS custom-properties spec, a property whose computed value cycles back to itself is 'guaranteed-invalid' and resolves to nothing wherever it is USED (there is no fallback in the `var(--radius-pill)` calls that consume it) — a definition-order bug, not a consumer bug. This lane writes no product code (dispatch: 'NO product code is written by this lane'); the fix (delete the redundant redeclaration at line 213, or point it at a differently-named canonical token) belongs to a product lane, flagged here with its exact line and mechanism per CLAUDE.md rule 13 ('a flag is a commitment'). FIXED by fix58-tokens (2026-09-07): theme.css's self-referential redeclaration removed; `--radius-pill` now resolves to 999px sitewide.

specs.source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/README.md §0.3 'The frame'; 'Caros Ledge UI System.dc.html' p1's nav-card block (section labels, active row, counts, footer)
notes: Sidebar.tsx's desktop nav card mixes inline style with Tailwind utility classes (`text-xl uppercase`, `text-[10px] font-bold tracking-[0.15em] uppercase`, etc. on the title/tagline). This harness injects `globals.css`/`theme.css` as RAW text without running Tailwind's build step (no PostCSS/Vite plugin — see mounts.mjs's STYLE_INJECT), so Tailwind's `@import "tailwindcss"` and its generated utility classes never resolve in this measured tree: a Tailwind-only property (e.g. the title's `text-xl` font-size) reads back as the browser's un-styled default, which is a HARNESS LIMITATION, not a product value — confirmed empirically (probed `aside.hidden > div:nth-child(2) h1` font-size: read 32px, the UA default h1 size, and text-transform: none, neither of which Sidebar.tsx's own inline style sets). This spec therefore asserts ONLY properties Sidebar.tsx sets via inline `style={}`, which bypass Tailwind entirely and are real regardless of this harness's raw-injection limitation. Title/tagline font-size, weight and text-transform (all Tailwind-class-driven in the desktop card) are NOT asserted here for that reason, not because they are known-correct.

The aside's own box model (width 252, margin, background, border, radius, band-gradient cap) is already covered by spec/page-frame.json's own top-level target on this same mount/selector; this spec adds the nav card's INTERNAL typography and active-state treatment, which page-frame.json does not touch.

dc.html p1 nav card active row ('Dashboard'): background #F5F2EE, `box-shadow: inset 3px 0 0 #5A5552` (an inset spine, not a border), font-weight 700. FIXED by fix58-tokens (2026-09-07, B96-B98): Sidebar.tsx's active row now uses that box-shadow spine (not `border-left`) and fontWeight 700 (not 800). Section-label letter-spacing (0.14em) and font-weight (700) were also unified across the card/drawer variants — the drawer variant already carried the correct values, only the desktop card diverged.

The mount's `next/navigation` stub (../smoke/stub-next-navigation.mjs, shared guard code, reused as-is per its own header) fixes `usePathname()` to `/community/smoke-test` — so `Sidebar.isActive()` marks COMMUNITY active (prefix match), not Dashboard, in this measured tree. The active-row targets below therefore select the Network section's Community row, not Brief's Dashboard row; this is a mount artefact of which item ends up `aria-current`, not of the STYLING those properties measure (the active-row style rule itself is identical regardless of which row it lands on).

rows.target: exactly one '+ Tag' trigger in the detail header (operator 3.2, mechanism repair train 58 2026-09-07)
rows.note: Operator 3.2: 'The action-row + Tag is the only trigger. Applied workspace tags still render as a row under the title; that row displays tags, it does not carry the trigger.' Moved out of `forbid` (train 58, 2026-09-07): a `forbid` entry can only assert absence (count 0), but the legitimate action-row trigger itself matches this selector, so a `forbid` here always read NOT IN SPEC at the correct count of 1 — a false positive on the passing state, not a real finding. Expressed instead as a `count: 1` target, which is what ruling 3.2 actually requires (a second trigger would measure count 2, a real MISMATCH). RESOLVED, fix58-tokens (2026-09-07): the count-5 reading was a HARNESS BUG, not a product defect. `targetsOf()`/`readTarget()` in run-audit.mjs carried `textMatch` through for `forbid` entries only; an ordinary target's or child's own `textMatch` field was silently dropped, so this row's selector ran as the bare `header:not(.cl-masthead) button` (every action-row button: the overflow '⋯', Export brief, Share, Watch, + Tag — five, not filtered to 'Tag' at all). Confirmed by a standalone debug mount dumping every matched button's textContent before the fix. Fixed at the root in run-audit.mjs (targetsOf, readTarget, and the probe() call-site mapping that had ALSO been dropping the field a second time — three places, not one — now all carry `textMatch` through for ordinary targets/children, not just `forbid`), not in this spec — the product's ActionRow already renders exactly one 'Tag'-labelled trigger, which is what a working count now measures.

rows.note: dc.html p15: `min-height:48px;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.06)`. Selector repair, train 58 (2026-09-07): the body (bodyPad) div holding NotificationPreferences is section's THIRD div child (after the rule div and the header div), not its second — `nth-child(2)` was reaching the header row itself, which has no `div` grandchild matching the rest of the chain, hence NOT BUILT. Confirmed by direct source read this session: NotifRow.tsx's real root div is `minHeight: 44` with `borderTop` (not `border-bottom`), on `var(--color-border-subtle)` — a genuine MISMATCH against the artboard's 48px/border-bottom, now that the check reaches the real element.
